::: home-intro
Two interactive lectures on how ‘omic’ data reveal what a drug does to a biological system, and where that picture can be misleading. Open a lecture to follow along in class, or jump to any activity to practice on your own.
:::

## Lectures {#lectures .home-heading}

::: home-lectures

::: {.home-lecture .home-lecture--one}
<p class="home-kicker">Lecture 1 · 50 minutes</p>

### Systems Pharmacology I: Transcriptomics {.home-lecture-title}

By the end of this lecture you should be able to:

- Distinguish systems biology, systems pharmacology, and systems toxicology.
- Interpret ‘omic’ signatures of disease states and drug responses.
- Use ‘omic’ signatures to identify drug targets and mechanisms of action.
- Evaluate drug efficacy and safety using systems pharmacology approaches.

[Open Lecture 1 →](lectures/lecture-01-showcase.html){.home-btn}
:::

::: {.home-lecture .home-lecture--two}
<p class="home-kicker">Lecture 2 · 50 minutes</p>

### Systems Pharmacology II: Single-Cell and Spatial {.home-lecture-title}

By the end of this lecture you should be able to:

- Explain how cellular heterogeneity impacts measurements of drug responses.
- Explain how tissue spatial organization impacts measurements of drug responses.
- Use cell-specific molecular signatures to evaluate and screen pharmacological responses.
- Compare cell-specific dose-response relationships to tissue-level measurements for evaluating drug efficacy and safety.

[Open Lecture 2 →](lectures/lecture-02-single-cell-spatial.html){.home-btn}
:::

:::

## Activities {#activities .home-heading}

::: home-intro
Each lecture is built around hands-on activities, one for each learning objective. They also run on their own, so you can come back to them for review.
:::

### Lecture 1 · Transcriptomics {.home-group .home-group--one}

::: home-activities

::: home-activity
<p class="home-lo">LO 1</p>

#### Systems Biology, Pharmacology, and Toxicology {.home-activity-title}

Switch the systems, pharmacology, and toxicology views on and off to see why one drug acting on one receptor leads to different outcomes in different organs.

[Open activity →](activities/systems-pharm-network/index.html)
:::

::: home-activity
<p class="home-lo">LO 2</p>

#### Understanding ‘Omic Signatures {.home-activity-title}

Predict, then reveal with real clustering: spot signatures, place an unknown drug, and match a disease signature to a candidate treatment.

[Open activity →](activities/omic-signatures/index.html)
:::

::: home-activity
<p class="home-lo">LO 3</p>

#### Mode of Action Discovery {.home-activity-title}

Pick two chemicals you think share a mode of action, check with clustering, then test the shared genes for pathway enrichment.

[Open activity →](activities/mode-of-action/index.html)
:::

::: home-activity
<p class="home-lo">LO 3</p>

#### Over-Representation or Ranked? {.home-activity-title}

Rank 20 genes, predict which pathway is enriched, then compare over-representation testing with a ranked method that uses the whole list.

[Open activity →](activities/enrichment-methods/index.html)
:::

::: home-activity
<p class="home-lo">LO 4</p>

#### From Gene Curves to a Dose {.home-activity-title}

Collapse 80 gene dose-response curves into a pathway-level point of departure, then weigh efficacy against safety.

[Open activity →](activities/pathway-point-of-departure/index.html)
:::

:::

#### Bulk or Mixed? Composition vs. State {.home-activity-title}

#### Screening by Cell-Specific Signature {.home-activity-title}

#### Cell-Specific vs. Tissue-Level Dose-Response {.home-activity-title}
